clue.text: Meat for each basket

parts.note: ham is a cured meat
per means for each, as in 'per head'

explanation.surface: A butcher's order: meat priced per item, packed into a basket.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamper is a large wicker basket with a lid, often for picnic food.

clue.text: The defence in a game a soldier introduced?

indicators.note: introduced means the soldier is put inside the run of a game a

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier is brought into a game to help the defence.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologia is a formal written justification of one's beliefs or conduct.

clue.text: Professional business cost divided by law

indicators.note: divided by means the cost is split open by the law placed within it

parts.note: price means cost
an act is a law passed by Parliament

explanation.surface: A firm's expenses are shared out according to legislation.
explanation.definitionFit: A practice is the business of a doctor, lawyer or other professional.

clue.text: Settle for about one thousand stickers by beginning of Easter

parts.note: re means about
I is the Roman numeral one
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
burs are prickly seed heads that stick to clothing

indicators.note: beginning of means take only the opening letter of Easter

explanation.surface: Agreeing to around a thousand labels by the start of Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: To reimburse is to repay, settling a debt.

clue.text: Dance student replacing master in madrigal, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps marks the reworked word as only one possible arrangement of its letters
replacing tells us one letter of the word madrigal is swapped for another

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for master, as in an MA degree
L is the learner-driver plate letter, standing for a student

explanation.surface: In a choral song, a student takes the place of the choirmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' swaps the M of MADRIGAL for L, giving LADRIGAL; 'perhaps' then rearranges those letters into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A galliard is a lively sixteenth-century court dance in triple time.

clue.text: Must a Sunday page misrepresent this writer?

indicators.note: misrepresent tells us the letters of the four words are set out falsely in a new order

explanation.surface: Would a newspaper's Sunday feature distort this author?
explanation.walkthrough: 'misrepresent' rearranges MUST A SUNDAY PAGE into the name of the French writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy de Maupassant was a nineteenth-century French short-story writer.

clue.text: No sailor escorted outside would wear this

indicators.note: outside means the escorted word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: led means escorted or guided
O is nought, nothing
tar is a traditional word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor taken out on the town would not be seen dead in this.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads with the whole clue: no sailor would wear this dancer's garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A leotard is a skintight one-piece garment worn by dancers and gymnasts.

clue.text: They say a girl studied a reptile

indicators.note: they say means the phrase is heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: a girl is A ANN and studied is conned, spoken as one run

explanation.surface: Gossip says a young woman examined a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, 'a Ann conned a' (conned meaning studied) sounds like the snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The anaconda is a large South American constrictor snake.

clue.text: Dawn's 24-hour holiday

parts.note: a day lasts twenty-four hours
a break is a short holiday

explanation.surface: A woman named Dawn has a one-day holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dawn's' looks like a woman's name with a possessive; it is the definition followed by 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Daybreak is the first light of morning.

clue.text: In yours truly's exam it constituted a drama

indicators.note: in places the exam and it inside the setter's own word for himself

parts.note: yours truly is the setter, giving MY as the possessive
an oral is a spoken examination
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone recalls that an exam of theirs took the form of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yours truly' is the crossword setter's way of saying 'me', so the possessive is 'my'; the morality play is a medieval genre.
explanation.definitionFit: A morality play is a medieval allegorical drama teaching virtue.

clue.text: Tongue made of gold returned by a host

indicators.note: returned means the heraldic word for gold is read backwards

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
a host is a great number, so many

explanation.surface: A speech woven from gold, handed back by a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'host' looks like someone throwing a party, but here it means a multitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Romany is the language spoken by the Roma people.

clue.text: Can be transported in carriage with the necessary power

parts.note: port is an old word for bearing or deportment, one's carriage
able means having the power to do something

explanation.surface: Something can be moved in a vehicle that has enough engine power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carriage' looks like a vehicle but means how one carries oneself, PORT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something portable is light enough to be carried around easily.

clue.text: Support for a small number surrounded by a smaller

indicators.note: surrounded by means the a and the smaller number sit within the small number

parts.note: four is a small number
V is the Roman numeral five, smaller than four's neighbour

explanation.surface: Backing given to a minor figure hemmed in by an even lesser one.
explanation.walkthrough: FOUR is cut open to hold A and V (Roman five), giving F-AV-OUR. Strictly five is bigger than four; the surface's 'smaller' plays on the numeral's single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To favour someone is to back or support them.

clue.text: New dairy cat a pillar of the Establishment?

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of dairy cat are made into something fresh

explanation.surface: A newly arrived farm cat is hailed as a pillar of society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges DAIRY CAT. The question mark flags that the pillar is literal: a stone column in a building, or establishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A caryatid is a carved female figure serving as a supporting column.

clue.text: Having arrived, dropped article from train — so natural!

parts.note: in means arrived, as a train is in

indicators.note: dropped means the article is let fall from the word train

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
sic is Latin for so or thus

explanation.surface: Arriving by train and leaving your newspaper piece behind feels natural.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped' removes A from TRAIN, leaving TRIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrinsic means inherent, belonging to a thing's essential nature.

clue.text: Liquor for a king confined in Kent, perhaps

indicators.note: confined in places the a and the king inside the region that Kent stands for

parts.note: Kent is a county in the south-east of England, so SE
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Drink is brought to a monarch kept captive in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England; 'perhaps' shows it is just one example of SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sake is Japanese rice wine, an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Unknown killer, having dispatched many

indicators.note: having dispatched means sending away one letter from the killer

parts.note: a strangler kills by choking
L is the Roman fifty, a large number

explanation.surface: A mystery murderer who has killed a lot of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispatched' hints at killing but here means sending away L (Roman fifty).
explanation.definitionFit: A stranger is someone unknown to you.

clue.text: Two books about prize plants

indicators.note: about means the two books go around the prize

parts.note: the Books of Kings are two books of the Old Testament
a cup is a trophy or prize

explanation.surface: A pair of gardening books on award-winning plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Kingcups are marsh marigolds, yellow-flowered wetland plants.

clue.text: Quantity of potatoes, say, to plunder

definitions.meaning: potatoes are sold by the large bag of a set weight

explanation.surface: A bag of spuds, or a raid on a town.
explanation.definitionFit: A sack is a large bag used as a measure of goods; to sack a city is to pillage it.

clue.text: Glass vessel covered once for travellers on the prairie

definitions.meaning: a tall glass for sherry or beer
a sailing ship with fore-and-aft rigging

definitions.text: covered once for travellers on the prairie
definitions.meaning: the covered wagon of American pioneers crossing the plains

explanation.surface: A glass container once kept covered for prairie pioneers.
explanation.definitionFit: Schooner names a large drinking glass, a two-masted ship, and the prairie wagon of settlers.

clue.text: Charge a smaller amount, being unconcerned

parts.note: care means charge, as in a child in one's care
less means a smaller amount

explanation.surface: Billing less money because you are not bothered.
explanation.definitionFit: Careless means heedless, not worried about consequences.

clue.text: Like some who rule? Absolutely

parts.note: describes rulers who govern with absolute, unchecked power, like a tyrant

explanation.definitionFit: Despotic means tyrannical, wielding absolute authority.

clue.text: Swimmer lacking the vitality of Marlborough's Lord Treasurer?

indicators.note: lacking means the statesman's name is without the vitality

parts.note: Sidney Godolphin was Lord Treasurer under Queen Anne, allied with the Duke of Marlborough
go means energy or vitality

explanation.surface: Was a historic statesman too sluggish to swim?
explanation.walkthrough: Godolphin was Queen Anne's Lord Treasurer, ally of the Duke of Marlborough; removing GO leaves the sea mammal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolphin is a marine mammal, a fast swimmer.

clue.text: Old coins for financial backers

definitions.meaning: the angel was an English gold coin of the 15th to 17th centuries
investors who fund a theatrical production

explanation.surface: Antique money changes hands among investors.
explanation.definitionFit: An angel was a historic English gold coin; backers of shows are also so called.

clue.text: Garment worn by fielder before bowling

indicators.note: before puts the fielder's word ahead of the bowling

parts.note: slip is a cricket fielding position beside the wicketkeeper
an over is a spell of six balls bowled in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricketer pulls on a jumper before bowling his spell.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, slip is a close fielding position and an over is a set of six balls bowled.
explanation.definitionFit: A slipover is a sleeveless pullover, a knitted top.

clue.text: Herdsman in state university church circle

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
O is shaped like a circle

explanation.surface: A cattleman is spotted in a church group at a state college.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaucho is a South American cowboy who herds cattle on the pampas.

clue.text: Serviceman posted to East Europe initially, not here

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, a naval serviceman
posted means sent, as by mail

indicators.note: initially means take only the opening letters of East and Europe

explanation.surface: A sailor sent off to Eastern Europe is consequently away.
explanation.definitionFit: An absentee is a person who is missing or away.

clue.text: Concerning boy worker contributing to the boom

parts.note: re means concerning or about
a son is a boy
a worker ant, the crossword's favourite worker

explanation.surface: Regarding a young man whose work feeds an economic boom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boom' suggests economic growth, but it is a deep resounding sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Something resonant reverberates, adding to a deep echoing sound.

clue.text: Leaders of 6 leave 18 in pet

indicators.note: leave means those letters depart from the other answer

parts.note: the answer to 18 down, meaning unconcerned
the first two letters of the answer to 6 down, a dancer's garment

explanation.surface: A cross-reference clue: parts of two other answers combine into a pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders of 6' are the first two letters of 6 down; 'leave' removes them from 18 down's answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To pet is to stroke or fondle affectionately.
